site.name: Mercury south pole, rule-selected high point (PGDA 88)
site.height_source: bilinear sample of PGDA 88 south-polar SfS DEM 250 m

rule.region: lat <= -88 (within 2 deg of the south pole)

frame.body_fixed_frame: Horizons: IAU_MERCURY (west-positive; converted to east-positive) = the IAU 2015 model (pck00011: W0 329.5988, Wdot 6.1385108 deg/d), identified by the T3 frame-tie test (Horizons quantity 14 reproduced to 1e-6 deg; the IAU 2009 model is off by 0.135 deg). MLA GDR: MESSENGER PCK pck00010_msgr_v21 (MLA RDR SIS), whose Mercury block (v2.0-2.3) has the same W0, Wdot and pole: MLA -> Horizons longitude offset 0 (science/worlds/frame_tie.py).
frame.model_3d: P = (R + h) [cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat], R = 2439400 m
frame.azimuth: degrees clockwise from LOCAL north (0 N, 90 E)
frame.elevation: degrees above the plane normal to the site radius vector (sphere normal)

datum.heights: metres above the 2439400 m reference sphere

flat_baseline.note: Flat-horizon control: mathematical horizon (0 deg) for every bin; smooth_sphere_dip_deg is the bare-sphere geometric dip at this observer height.

skyline.method: great-circle rays on the world sphere, each DEM layer sampled bilinearly in its own grid (priority fill), body-fixed 3D elevation vs the sphere normal, single ray per bin centre, no refraction
skyline.label: SOURCE-BASED UNVALIDATED

curvature_limit.formula: theta_max(e) = acos((R + h_eye) cos e / (R + H)) - e ; L = R theta_max ; L_req = max over bins L(e_bin)
curvature_limit.relief_source: Measured 2026-11-16 on the downloaded products, heights above 2 439.4 km: USGS DEM 665 m v2 -5 382 to +4 497 m (Becker et al. 2016, LPSC 47 #2959); MLA hdem_75n_250m -5 651 to +2 692 m. Bounds +5.1 / -5.7 km include margin (checked in science/worlds/tests/test_mercury_data.py).
curvature_limit.note: Bins below beyond_range_world_bound_elev_deg could still be raised by terrain <= H_world_max_m beyond max_range_m (world-wide bound; a conservative flag, not a detected obstruction).

dem_layers.note: m above 2 439.4 km (file name; checked against USGS)

metrics.label: SOURCE-BASED UNVALIDATED

method.visible_pct: share of hourly Horizons samples (both endpoints included) with the body centre above the skyline (perpendicular margin > 0); NO bisection refinement (any-site default)
method.longest_hidden_h: longest run of consecutive hidden hourly samples x step_h
method.disk_mean: trapezoid over hourly samples of the visible-disk fraction
method.unknown: samples over no-data skyline bins count as hidden

metrics.disclaimer: Local geometric visibility only: not certified illumination, power, or DSN link availability.
metrics.window_label: one solar day (176 d = 2 Mercury years)

sources.description: JPL Horizons observer tables CENTER=coord@199 (CYLINDRICAL site), QUANTITIES=4,13,20, APPARENT=AIRLESS

limitations: Local geometric terrain visibility only; not certified illumination/power or DSN telecom availability.
Single ray per 0.5 deg azimuth bin at the bin centre; sub-bin peaks can be missed.
Hourly samples, no bisection refinement of crossings.
Horizons az/el (ellipsoid normal) rotated to the sphere normal used by the skyline.
Product members are alternative terrain products, not calibrated probabilities.
Requirements copied from the Moon team as ENGINEERING ASSUMPTIONS unless the world states its own.
PGDA 88 SfS DEM 250 m: shape-from-shading on MDIS NAC images adjusted to MLA; its own accuracy statement is in the Zenodo record (not re-derived here).
The site is a rule-selected high point, not a surveyed landing site.

world.name: mercury
world.shape: sphere R = 2 439 400 m for heights and rays (IAU 2015 mean radius; the MLA/USGS map-projection sphere). Horizons uses an ellipsoid 2440.53/2440.53/2438.26 km; the site is passed in cylindrical coordinates so that its radius is exact. MLA hdem_75n_250m heights are relative to 2 440 000 m and are re-referenced (+600 m).
world.body_fixed_frame: Horizons: IAU_MERCURY (west-positive; converted to east-positive) = the IAU 2015 model (pck00011: W0 329.5988, Wdot 6.1385108 deg/d), identified by the T3 frame-tie test (Horizons quantity 14 reproduced to 1e-6 deg; the IAU 2009 model is off by 0.135 deg). MLA GDR: MESSENGER PCK pck00010_msgr_v21 (MLA RDR SIS), whose Mercury block (v2.0-2.3) has the same W0, Wdot and pole: MLA -> Horizons longitude offset 0 (science/worlds/frame_tie.py).

comms.label: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION

relays.description: no Mercury relay exists; direct-to-Earth only

comms.definition: Earth centre above the terrain skyline (hourly sample) AND not in a superior-conjunction outage (geocentric SEP < threshold)

conjunctions.source: DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook 810-005, module 106 "Solar Corona and Solar Wind Effects", Rev. B (30 Sep 2010), section 2.3: standard downlink BPSK link design and coding achieve X-band data return at SEP angles down to at least 2.3 deg, and Ka-band down to 1 deg. https://deepspace.jpl.nasa.gov/dsndocs/810-005/106/106B.pdf
conjunctions.label: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION
conjunctions.note: Outage = superior conjunction with SEP below the X-band threshold (coronal scintillation, module 106). Inferior conjunctions below the threshold put the Sun near the ground antenna beam (noise, module 105): flagged, not assessed, not counted as outage.

comms.threshold_source: DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook 810-005, module 106 "Solar Corona and Solar Wind Effects", Rev. B (30 Sep 2010), section 2.3: standard downlink BPSK link design and coding achieve X-band data return at SEP angles down to at least 2.3 deg, and Ka-band down to 1 deg. https://deepspace.jpl.nasa.gov/dsndocs/810-005/106/106B.pdf
comms.not_modelled: DSN station elevation and scheduling, link budget, Sun-in-beam noise at inferior conjunction, antenna pointing; any atmosphere effect on the link.
